mainEntity.name: How much does it cost to replace a GLA 200 or GLA 250 petrol engine in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A GLA 200 or GLA 250 petrol engine replacement typically costs between £1,500 and £4,200 depending on condition type and whether fitting is included. M270 1.6L and 2.0L units range from £1,500 to £4,200 supply only. Rebuilt M270 (GLA 200 / 250): £1,500-£4,200 supply only. Reconditioned units: £1,800-£3,500. Used engines from breakers: £1,200-£3,200 but higher risk. Labour for supply & fit adds £800-£1,500 to any engine price.

mainEntity.name: Is the M270 engine in the GLA 200 and 250 reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M270 is considered a fundamentally sound engine, with 200,000 km examples common across all platforms. However, it has predictable weak points that are entirely manageable with the right maintenance approach. Timing chain stretch and tensioner wear from 80,000-100,000 miles. High-pressure fuel pump failure on higher-mileage units. Carbon buildup on intake valves (inherent to direct injection). Camshaft actuator wear causing ticking on cold start. Post-2014 engines have improved chain tensioners and engine management.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of M270 timing chain failure in a GLA petrol?

acceptedAnswer.text: The M270's timing chain system typically shows warning signs before complete failure. Rattling or clanking noise on cold start lasting 1-3 seconds. Rough idle and loss of power. Check engine light with cam/crank correlation fault codes. Metallic ticking noise from the engine when warm. If ignored, the chain can jump teeth and destroy the engine.

mainEntity.name: Should I repair or replace my GLA 200 or 250 petrol engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Repair if the failure is isolated (e.g., timing chain tensioner, HPFP, camshaft actuators, carbon cleaning). Replace if there's bottom end damage, bore scoring, or catastrophic timing chain failure. Timing chain replacement at specialist: £1,100-£1,700 - do this at first sign of rattle. HPFP replacement: £500-£800 - do this immediately after first cut-out. Walnut blasting: £300-£500 - preventative every 60,000 miles. Full M270 rebuild: £2,800-£4,200 - for catastrophic failure or 100k+ miles. Given GLA values (£8,000-£18,000), a rebuilt engine is typically good value.

mainEntity.name: How do I know which engine code my GLA 200 or 250 has?

acceptedAnswer.text: Check your vehicle log book (V5C) for the engine number, which includes the engine code prefix. V5C log book shows full engine number with code prefix. Engine code stamped on cylinder block. GLA 200 (2013-2020): M270.910 (M270 DE16 AL, 1.6L, 156hp). GLA 250 (2013-2020): M270.920 (M270 DE20 AL, 2.0L, 211hp). Service history documents list engine type.

mainEntity.name: Can I fit a used GLA 200 or 250 petrol engine myself?

acceptedAnswer.text: We strongly advise against DIY fitting on a GLA petrol. The transverse-mounted engine layout, 7G-DCT gearbox alignment, and ECU coding requirements demand specialist equipment and expertise. Transverse engine mounting requires specialist alignment. 7G-DCT transmission alignment needs precise setup. ECU coding and immobiliser synchronisation required. Specialist supply & fit costs £800-£1,500 - worth every penny.

GLA 250 launched with M270 DE20 AL 2.0L turbo petrol, 211hp, 350Nm torque, 7G-DCT automatic as standard
GLA 250 4MATIC introduced with all-wheel drive and 2.0L M270 engine
Facelift with revised styling, engine line-up unchanged
X156 production ends, H247 second-generation replaces M270 with M282 (1.3L) and M260 (2.0L) engines

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes Benz GLA Class 200 / 250 Petrol Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Mercedes Benz GLA 200 and GLA 250 rely on the M270 petrol engine family - generally smooth and efficient when properly maintained, but with well-documented vulnerabilities. Timing chain stretch, high-pressure fuel pump failure, camshaft actuator wear, and carbon buildup on intake valves are the most frequently cited issues. Every rebuilt engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded components designed to address the original failure point - plus a minimum 12-month unlimited mileage warranty. Below we break down the most common GLA petrol engine failures, what they cost to fix, and when replacement is the smarter financial decision.

problems.h4: M270 Timing Chain Stretch - Why the GLA 200 / 250 Rattles on Cold Start
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes Benz GLA Class GLA 200 (M270 DE16 AL) and GLA 250 (M270 DE20 AL), 2013-2020
problems.rootCause: The M270 uses a dual-stage timing chain system that requires more attention than a single-chain setup. Insufficient oil pressure during cold starts, combined with chain guide wear, leads to elongation of the chain. Once the tensioner exceeds its adjustment range, chain slap produces the characteristic rattle on cold start. If ignored, the chain can jump teeth with catastrophic valve-piston contact.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain tensioner and guides only, oil and filter change
repairOptions.longevity: 60k-80k miles. Only viable if chain has not stretched significantly

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace timing chain, tensioner, guides, sprockets, and camshaft actuators
repairOptions.longevity: 80k-100k miles. Corrects the root cause properly

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt M270 with new timing components, chain, and upgraded tensioner
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty. Required if chain has jumped

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical GLA 200 or GLA 250 (X156) is worth £8,000-£18,000 depending on age, mileage and condition - the full replacement cost of £2,800-£4,200 is modest relative to vehicle value for most examples. For vehicles worth under £8,000, evaluate repair options first.
problems.recommendation: If your GLA 200 or 250 rattles for 1-2 seconds on cold start, catch it early with a specialist chain replacement (£1,100-£1,700) - this is far cheaper than waiting for full engine failure. On a car with over 100,000 miles, a full rebuilt engine with upgraded timing components often delivers better long-term value than spending £1,100-£1,700 on repairs that leave a high-mileage bottom end in place.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M270 Mercedes Benz GLA Class 200 / 250 engine prices

problems.h4: M270 High-Pressure Fuel Pump Failure - Why the GLA 200 / 250 Cuts Out Suddenly
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes Benz GLA Class GLA 200 (M270 DE16 AL) and GLA 250 (M270 DE20 AL), 2013-2020
problems.rootCause: The M270 uses a camshaft-driven high-pressure fuel pump (HPFP) located on top of the cylinder head that operates at up to 200 bar. Internal wear - particularly to the pump piston and cam follower - reduces fuel pressure to the direct injection rails, triggering limp mode or complete engine cut-out. Contaminated fuel accelerates wear. This issue is documented in Mercedes TSB 07.01.15.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace HPFP, flush fuel system, replace fuel filter, clear fault codes
repairOptions.longevity: 80k-100k miles. Suitable when caught immediately after first cut-out

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: HPFP replacement plus injector testing and rail inspection for metal debris
repairOptions.longevity: 80k-100k miles. Required if HPFP has contaminated the fuel rail

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt M270 with new HPFP, injectors, high-pressure rails, and timing components
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty. Necessary when metal debris has destroyed camshaft lobes

problems.vehicleValueCheck: On a GLA 200 or 250 worth £8,000-£18,000, the HPFP replacement at £500-£800 is a sensible repair. Full engine replacement is only justified if metal debris has caused additional damage.
problems.recommendation: If your GLA 200 or 250 has cut out once but restarted, don't gamble. Replace the HPFP at a specialist immediately - £500-£800 is far cheaper than replacing injectors or an entire engine. On higher-mileage M270 units with over 90,000 miles, a full rebuilt engine with new HPFP and timing components eliminates all common failure points in one go.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M270 Mercedes Benz GLA Class 200 / 250 engine prices

problems.group: M270 Carbon Buildup & Camshaft Actuator Wear
problems.h4: M270 Carbon Buildup & Camshaft Actuator Wear - Why the GLA Petrol Loses Power
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes Benz GLA Class GLA 200 (M270 DE16 AL) and GLA 250 (M270 DE20 AL), 2013-2020
problems.rootCause: The M270's direct injection system means fuel does not wash the intake valves, allowing carbon deposits to accumulate over time. This leads to misfires, rough idle, and loss of power. Additionally, camshaft actuator wear (part A2700501147) can cause ticking on cold start - and on certain model years (particularly 2015), inadequately welded camshafts can fail catastrophically.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Walnut blast intake valves, clean throttle body, reset adaptations
Replace camshaft actuators (Y49/1, Y49/2) with updated parts
repairOptions.longevity: 80k-100k miles. If ticking on cold start or fault codes present

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace camshafts, actuators, timing chain components
repairOptions.longevity: 100k+ miles. Required if camshaft welding failure has occurred

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Supply & fit rebuilt M270 with new camshafts, actuators, and upgraded components
repairOptions.longevity: Full long-block warranty. Necessary for catastrophic camshaft failure

problems.vehicleValueCheck: On a GLA 200 or 250 worth £8,000-£18,000, walnut blasting at £300-£500 is excellent preventative maintenance. Camshaft actuator replacement at £450-£750 is also justified. Full engine replacement is only necessary for catastrophic failure.
problems.recommendation: The M270's carbon buildup is an inherent trait of direct-injection petrol engines - budget for walnut blasting every 60,000 miles to maintain performance and fuel economy. If you hear ticking on cold start, have the camshaft actuators inspected immediately; updated parts (A2700501147) resolve the issue. For 2015 model year M270 engines, have the camshafts inspected - inadequate welding has been documented on this production year.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M270 Mercedes Benz GLA Class 200 / 250 engine prices

problems.h4: M270 Dual-Mass Flywheel Rattle - Misdiagnosed As Engine Fault on GLA 250
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes Benz GLA Class GLA 250 (M270 DE20 AL, 2013-2020, 7G-DCT)
problems.rootCause: The dual-mass flywheel (DMF) on 7G-DCT equipped GLA 250 models uses two masses separated by spring dampers. Over time, the springs weaken and the flywheel develops excessive rotational play. The resulting rattle at idle and vibration during gear changes is frequently misdiagnosed as timing chain tensioner noise or internal engine knock.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace dual-mass flywheel and flex plate

repairOptions.tier: Intermediate - DMF Plus Rear Main Seal
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: DMF replacement plus crankshaft rear main seal and gearbox input shaft seal
DMF is a transmission-out repair only

problems.vehicleValueCheck: On a GLA 250 worth £8,000-£18,000, DMF replacement at £700-£1,100 is a sensible repair.
problems.recommendation: Before authorising any timing chain work on a rattling GLA 250, insist a specialist checks the dual-mass flywheel first. DMF replacement at a transmission specialist costs £700-£1,100; an unnecessary engine rebuild because a mechanic misdiagnosed flywheel chatter as timing chain failure costs £2,800-£4,200. If your GLA 250 has over 80,000 miles and you're keeping it long-term, replace the rear main seal while the gearbox is off - the part is cheap and the labour is already covered.
